expanded_body:
Originally posted March 16, 2026.

No affidavit. A business shut down. Assets frozen. Hundreds of employees displaced. Is this how due process works?

Doug Polk finally broke his silence on The Lodge Card Club raid, and what he revealed should concern every Texas poker player.

In his written statement, Polk emphasized that he did not participate in, and had no knowledge of, any money laundering in the operation of The Lodge, while pledging that members with chip balances and tournament payouts would be made whole in coordination with his attorneys.

The most important line in his entire statement? "That affidavit has not been given to the Lodge or made public."

The people whose business was shut down didn't even know the specific allegations against them at that point. No arrests. No charges. Just a closed door and hundreds of employees out of work.

A search warrant is not a conviction. But right now it's being treated like one.

I would love to hear your thoughts and opinions on this ongoing issue.

— Sham
author: Shomari Williams

fact_verification_flags.claim: Doug Polk released a public written statement on March 16, 2026 stating that the search-warrant affidavit had not been given to The Lodge or made public
fact_verification_flags.note: Verified by attached screenshot of Doug Polk's verified Facebook post (images/2026-03-16_2.jpg).

outdated_info_flags.original_statement: That affidavit has not been given to The Lodge or made public
outdated_info_flags.current_status: The 22-page affidavit was subsequently released on March 17, 2026; a Williamson County grand jury returned a no-bill on April 28, 2026, and The Lodge reopened in May 2026
outdated_info_flags.editorial_note: Describes conditions on March 16, 2026 prior to the March 17 release of the affidavit.
